concepts.title: Общий проём и две согласованные проекции
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: architectural game-design illustration for a 2.5D side-scrolling survival game, one standalone frame, landscape 1536x1024.
Visual style: detailed painterly game environment, distressed Russian apartment shelter after a war, cracked green-grey plaster, exposed brown brick patches, worn timber floor, subdued grey daylight with clear readable midtones, charcoal cutaway structure, restrained teal and warm brown palette. Polished production concept art, not photorealistic and not cute. Legible architecture takes priority over darkness. No interface, no icons, no title, no labels, no captions, no arrows, no text, no watermarks. No people.
The design problem is to allow doors on BOTH left and right boundaries of a room while movement is horizontal across the screen. DO NOT put any door in the rear wall. Show a centered room with a small broken rear window, a low weathered workbench directly under the window and a few brick fragments. Center room occupies 70 percent of the width. Show narrow fragments of the adjoining room on each side, so the two left/right door connections really join adjacent rooms. No other doors, no stairs, no ceiling lights. Black rough cutaway slabs at top and bottom. Both doors should be large, readable architectural features. The entire room fits within frame. For each of these two portals, closed means physically blocks horizontal travel; open means continuous floor is visible through the side threshold.

Design 1, CLOSED STATE. Keep a fixed frontal dollhouse camera. Every room has a shallow one-point perspective towards its own center; the left and right short side walls of the main room are both visible and taper toward the back wall. Install an ordinary weathered wooden hinged door into EACH of the two side walls, both fully CLOSED. Left and right doorway assemblies are geometrically mirrored and equally legible. Important architectural convention: the physical wall junction belongs to both adjoining rooms. Each shared portal gets a matching room-facing surface on either side of the charcoal cut edge, two views of the same door, not two sequential doors. Render closed wooden surfaces meeting at the boundary to accommodate both room perspectives. Frames, top lintels and continuous threshold align between adjacent rooms. No massive black column covering the portal. Doors remain physically in side-wall planes, diagonally foreshortened, not frontal decorative panels on rear wall. Broad closed faces and brass handles visible from the main room. Symmetric framing. A close study of sensible double-sided shared doorway geometry.
